title: Plan the talk
pitch: About 4 minutes. A hard talk tends to end the way it starts, so this helps you plan a soft opening, the one thing you want heard, and how to pause before it turns into a fight.

cards.prompt: About 4 minutes. A hard talk tends to end the way it starts, so this helps you plan a soft opening, the one thing you want heard, and how to pause before it turns into a fight.
How do you feel right now?
cards.why: A number now lets you see whether planning took some of the dread out.

cards.prompt: What's the talk about, and who is it with?
cards.why: Putting it in one place shows you what this talk is really for.

cards.short: what I want them to hear
cards.prompt: If they remember one thing you said, what should it be?
cards.why: Knowing your one point keeps the talk from drifting into old fights.

cards.prompt: Write your opening like this: I feel… about… and I need…
cards.why: Starting with how you feel, not what they did, makes it easier for them to listen.
Spotting the hot spot ahead of time lets you catch it before it catches you.

cards.prompt: How will you know you're too worked up to keep going?
cards.why: Knowing your own signs tells you when to pause while you still can.

cards.prompt: Write the line you'll say to take a break, with a time to come back. Something like: I need 20 minutes, then let's keep going.
cards.why: Having the words ready makes a break feel like care instead of walking out.

cards.prompt: How ready do you feel for it?
cards.why: It tells you whether to plan a little more or go have the talk.

cards.prompt: How do you feel right now?
cards.why: Comparing with the start shows you what having a plan did.
